author: .just_kk
content:
This is +1 argument for having  topic with global aggregates proving every slot committee.

Aggregators of the slot following the missed slot will be able to recursively aggregate the global proof from the missed slot into their subnet or global proof (leanVM is capable of doing recursive aggregation of proofs with different attestation data)

As long as at least one aggregator performs such aggregation we are good. Such proof should be considered as better proof than just proof for the current slot attestations when it is picked by next proposer

author: m.kalinin
content:
My codex is saying that 28 subnets with 1 aggregator each, 1 second for attestation broadcast then 3 seconds for aggregation and then 5 seconds to broadcast aggregates would be the most optimal in terms of bandwidth consumption between the attestation and aggregation phases -- they are almost even; I know it's a bad metric but that's at least something. I am using the time to aggregate and the size of aggregates from the <#1572284542990155908> . The closest would be 32 subnets and 1 aggregate, it slightly worse at the aggregation bandwidth part.

16 subnets gives a worse result because it takes more time to produce an aggregate thus less time for the broadcast

author: yannvonlanthen
content:
On this, my current view is that with DC we can reduce network load in three meaningful ways: 

1. Vote from the start of the slot, so we gain 3s per slot (with Gasper worst case attestation propagation start at t=3s)
2. We can pipeline, so no more dead time on the network while aggregation happens - and no more dead time on CPU while aggregations are broadcast
3. We can afford to have more optimistic assumptions, without negative impact on fork choice: For example, we can have less aggregators, and if an aggregate is missing, later aggregators can pick up the slack

author: .just_kk
content:
Previously we discussed that only subnet aggregators are eligible to produce global proofs with assumption that with 4 aggregators per subnet we will have some aggregator with high stake which is subscribed to all subnets anyway.

If we switch to 1 aggregator per subnet I am not sure if that assumption still holds, so we might need to rethink who is eligible to produce the global proof

author: vladimir_ea
content: oh i see, so 1 of 16 is subscribed to all and aggregates all? The issue with this I think is that even if you have 64 cores or something on your machine  you still cannot do 16 leaf aggregations in parallel b/c memory bandwidth becomes a bottleneck. A single leaf aggregation on leanVM currently reads / writes ~25GB/s to RAM which is approaching limits on most motherboards.

author: vladimir_ea
content: so such large operators would need to be able to partition this work across multiple machines.

author: m.kalinin
content: oh, I didn't know about that limitation

author: vladimir_ea
content: it seems like for both the leaf aggregations and the 16->1 it should be safe to use 'outside help' if it is available. Source the attestation aggregate from a large operator / provider - take the intersection of the attestations / clams you have and the aggregate has - verify the proof with the declared claims - this last produces a new proof but it is much faster then aggregating (~200ms or similar).
